title: blind judge batch output (NNN.out.json)
description: The contract between `eval-judge` and `brain eval judge merge` (spec §5.2 layer 3, §5.4). Every case is BLIND: `case_id` and `pair_id` are random labels, and the map from a label back to a retrieval strategy lives in data/eval/blind_map.json, which is written outside the batch directory and which you never read. Two arrays because a batch carries two kinds of work: `scores[]` answers a single case on the four rubric metrics of brain/eval/rubric.md, and `pairs[]` picks a winner between two anonymous answers to one question. `scores` is always required (it may be an empty array); `pairs` may be omitted entirely by a judge whose batch carried no pairwise case, but a batch that omits it while carrying pairwise cases has those cases reported as unjudged. Merge applies this file in two halves: the ENVELOPE (`batch_id`, both arrays being arrays, no unknown top-level field) decides whether the batch is readable at all, and a batch that fails it goes to `retry/` and then to `quarantine/`; everything under `$defs` is checked per record, so one bad judgment is rejected and counted while the rest of the batch merges. Rules merge adds that a schema cannot state: a `case_id` must be a case of the matching `.in.json`; a metric may be null ONLY when that case declares the metric does not apply (`context_available: false` makes faithfulness null, and then it MUST be null); and `justification` must contain a verbatim quotation in double quotes — a score with no quoted evidence is an opinion and is reported as one.

batch_id.description: Exactly the `batch_id` of the .in.json this answers, e.g. "shard-01/007".

scores.description: One entry per `cases[]` entry of the input, in any order. Empty only when the batch has no single cases. A case you leave out is reported as unjudged, which reads as the strategy behind it having no layer-3 number at all.

pairs.description: One entry per `pairwise[]` entry of the input, in any order. Empty, or absent, only when the batch has no pairwise cases — a pairwise case with no entry here is reported as unjudged, and the strategy comparison it was meant to settle simply does not happen.

notes.description: Free-text remarks for the planner — a gold answer that looks wrong, a question two answers read differently. Never a place to hide a rule you could not follow: that is a `failed` entry in status.json.

metric.description: 0, 1 or 2 by the rubric in brain/eval/rubric.md. `null` ONLY for a metric the case declares inapplicable — today that is faithfulness on a case with `context_available: false`, where no packed context was recorded and there is nothing to be faithful to. Never null because you found it hard to decide: that is a 1.

justification.description: Why these scores, in two to four sentences, containing at least one VERBATIM quotation in double quotes — from the answer when you are marking it down, from the context or the gold answer when you are saying what is missing. Copy the words; never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. English, whatever the answer's language.

case_id.description: The opaque label of the case, copied exactly from the input. It carries no meaning; do not try to read one into it.

unsupported_claims.description: Every claim in the answer that the context does not support, quoted verbatim from the answer. Empty when there are none. This is the evidence behind the faithfulness score, so a faithfulness below 2 with an empty list is reported as unevidenced.

answer_language_ok.description: Optional. False when the answer is not in the language the case declares (`lang`). Scored separately from the rubric — a correct answer in the wrong language is still correct — and reported on its own.

pair_id.description: The opaque label of the pairwise case, copied exactly from the input.

winner.description: Which of the two answers serves the asker better, judged against `gold_answer` and the question — `a`, `b`, or `tie` when neither is better on the facts. The order of `a` and `b` was randomised, so it says nothing; never prefer the longer answer, and never prefer the one that sounds more confident.

both_wrong.description: Optional. True when neither answer contains the gold fact. A `tie` with `both_wrong: true` and a `tie` between two correct answers are opposite results, and the report separates them.
